chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fear the injustice, for it is the darknesses of the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of injustice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith utilizes the metaphor of 'darkness' (zulumat) to illustrate how injustice obscures the soul's perception of divine truth, a concept deeply explored in Shia tafsir as both a spiritual and physical reality on the Day of Resurrection. It underscores the gravity of oppression not merely as a social sin but as a fundamental barrier to light (nur) and guidance, warning believers that their own actions create the shadows they will navigate in the afterlife.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Mansour, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Fear the injustice for it would be a darkness on the Day of Judgment’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mansur from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Be afraid of doing injustice; on the Day of Judgment there will be much darkness.’”
